cells.tense: The ending is already here, and the pen is steady in the hand now.
cells.ask: Think of one role you keep playing for someone that stopped fitting a while back. Set it down where they'll notice, and let the space stay open. No reasoning with them about it this week.
cells.core:
You feel what people carry, and you notice when something between you has finished. A room doesn't need soothing before it can be cleared. Grief and release can share an afternoon. Holding the feeling around an ending doesn't have to keep the ending going.

Find something you're still carrying for someone that's already over — a request you keep answering, a way of showing up nobody asks for anymore. Put it down where they can see. Then let it stay down. Any reason you'd give would just be another way of holding on. The clearing happens because your hands come off it. What comes next arrives when it arrives.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel the room and still clear away a thing.
cells.verb: Tending the felt space between people

cells.tense: The next ending will arrive already rehearsed in your head before it happens.
cells.act: maintain the abundance by clearing what is finished
cells.ask: Notice a goodbye you're managing that nobody has said yet. Keep your hands off it this week — no early clearing, no quiet preparing, no bracing them for what hasn't happened. Just watch what the week does with it.
cells.core:
You read a shift between people before anyone says it. Lately you're ending things that finished only in your own mind — a friendship closed off on a Tuesday, an exit planned for a job you still have. The far-seeing has turned into rehearsal, and the rehearsal keeps you from being where you actually are. The person with you gets the emptied version, already three steps past.

What is finished is the only thing to clear. Pick one ending you've been pre-loading. Keep your hands off it this week. No preparing the other person, no soft exit, no clearing the ground early. If it's truly done, it will end without the rush. If it isn't, you've kept something. Either way you'll have watched a real thing instead of a script you wrote.

cells.tense: The door closed behind you, and the room ahead got only part of you.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Pick an ending where your piece went unsaid. Write the true sentence to that person — what you needed at the time, plainly — and don't send it. Put the page somewhere it stops asking for a reply.
cells.core:
Sitting with another person's feeling is what you do well. Somewhere along the way you stepped out of that and didn't fully step back in. You arrive and something in you has already gone ahead. Not unkind — just not entirely here. The people close to you can feel the distance, and the distance isn't about them.

One ending still has something you never got to say. Gather it into a sentence: what you needed at the time, in your own words. Write it to them and don't send it. Say it to the page once. Then put the page somewhere it stops asking for a reply. That sentence belongs to you, and the writing is how you take it back. The next room is available after that.

cells.tense: The ending is under way, and whatever pattern is in it has been running unnamed.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Write the last three endings as lines: what happened, in order, no feeling words. Read the three back and find the word they already share. Circle it if one shows up. That's the whole job for now.
cells.core:
You have a way of seeing through the surface of a thing to the shape underneath. That way of seeing has been running on a pattern in your own life — endings you didn't choose, people who shifted, roles that stopped fitting — and it's been running unnamed. The sameness may have been visible before. It hasn't been called yours.

The move is to cut to the structure. Take the last three endings and write a line for each: what actually happened, no feeling words on the page. Read them back. Find the word the three already share, if there is one, and circle it. That word is not the story you'd tell anyone about it. You may not like it, and there's nothing to act on today. A pattern with a name is one you can walk out of.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the Balanced person already trusts the endings (I wrote 'you can feel it and still trust the ending' — the record doesn't say they trust it, only that the capacity is operating correctly there). A reader could reasonably say 'I feel it and I still brace.' The ask survives a wrong read: if they aren't free of bracing, sitting one night with an ending that has already happened still teaches them what fear is doing. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'without flinching' — it admires the person for a method; I cut it and wrote 'before you move to fix it.' I also kept the Cardinal backend out: no house names, no 'compassion,' no 'transformation' as a label.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in status 4 is that the person can already see the pattern and is looking past it — the record only says they're operating without conscious integration, not that they know. I cut 'you already know' and left the question genuinely open. The reader's likely objection in status 1 is 'I don't feel free of bracing at all' — but the ask is not conditional on feeling free, so it still teaches them where the grief sits if the read is wrong. The sentence that served me more than them was 'without flinching' and the tidy closing image in status 1; both are gone. Status 3's ask is the one I'm least sure survives a wrong read, since if the person is still in contact with the person they're mourning, saying what they needed out loud is awkward — but it harms nothing and shows them something either way.
